survey: A toy planetary rover in a three-quarter view from slightly above. We see its long left side almost square-on and its right end strongly foreshortened. The orange box body has an inset lid on top; the lid's top face is visible at a moderate angle, which matches the high camera. A vertical steel mast stands on the lid and holds a gold dish tilted toward the viewer; the dish's open rim ellipse fits that tilt, and the orange feed knob comes out of the dish's centre. A second short vertical mast holds a solar panel tilted up toward the camera. Its 2×3 grid of cells runs parallel to the panel's frame edges. On the side panel, the riveted plate and the three vent slots face the camera, which suits a side seen nearly square-on. The right end panel narrows correctly. Steel suspension legs come from one main pivot in the middle of the side and a smaller secondary pivot, and splay down and out to three near wheels. Three far-side wheels show between and behind them, set higher and further back. The near wheels are near-circular, which fits a side that faces the camera. Their hub caps sit slightly left of each wheel's centre, which fits a camera off to the right that also shows the right end of the body. Along the row the wheel bottoms slope down to the right more steeply than the body's bottom edge. That is correct: lines further below the horizon converge more steeply. The wheels get slightly larger toward the nearer right end. All wheels rest on the grey rolling ground with contact shadows, at the angle the ground is drawn. Both masts are vertical and parallel to the body's vertical edges.
